clue.text: Entertainment drawn from a game a lot, performance of redcoat welcomed

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matchsticks or counters from piles

indicators.note: the shuffled redcoat is taken in by the other piece, as a guest is welcomed indoors

parts.note: a ton is informal for a great quantity

indicators.note: a performance of the word redcoat puts its letters through a routine, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A holiday-camp redcoat's show gets a warm welcome, the entertainment drawn from a game played a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance of' rearranges the letters of redcoat, and 'welcomed' sets them inside A TON. A redcoat is an entertainer at a Butlin's holiday camp. 'drawn' means made of drawings, not pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn entertainment is a film made from a sequence of drawings, the classic form of animation.

clue.text: Sensing money, belt out to secure it

indicators.note: the singing holds the coin fast inside itself, securing it

parts.note: to belt out a song is to sing it loudly
a cent is a small coin, so a piece of money

explanation.surface: Someone who smells cash starts singing to grab it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe detecting something, by smell or by intuition, as in smelling victory.

clue.text: English novelist fighting to be heard?

indicators.note: the word is spoken rather than written, so its sound gives a name spelt differently

parts.note: fighting between nations is war

explanation.surface: Asks whether some English writer can be heard brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech the R of 'war' is silent, so it sounds just like the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh, author of Brideshead Revisited, was an English writer of novels.

clue.text: Major route in shreds, moved away

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written here with the figure as the letter I
cheese that has been grated is in shreds

explanation.surface: A main road torn to pieces, as if the traffic had moved elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords often read its 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds or people who have relocated to another region have done so seasonally or permanently.

clue.text: Get out snooker equipment shortly, then what's on it?

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the rest is the cross-headed stick used to support a cue for a long shot
a cue is what lies on the rest when it is used

explanation.surface: A snooker player told to fetch the rest and then whatever sits upon it.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the rest supports the cue, which is why the cue is 'what's on it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from danger or a trap is to save them, getting them out.

clue.text: Notorious wolf introduced to flock, any ewes terrified!

indicators.note: the name has been slipped in among the words that follow, tucked inside the flock of letters

explanation.surface: A wolf gets in among the sheep and the ewes panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'flock' to the start of 'terrified'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American rapper is famous for public outbursts, and a wolf is a predatory man, so the label fits his notoriety.

clue.text: Basically bitter wind up for worker outdoors

indicators.note: in a down light the base of a word is its bottom letter, its last

parts.note: to wind someone up is to irritate or anger them

explanation.surface: An outdoor worker gets bitter and wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: A park or forest warden patrols open country, so works out of doors.

clue.text: Spirit of the Far East seen ordering — this?

parts.note: chi is the vital life force in Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: putting the word seen into a new order rearranges its letters

parts.note: the dash read as a minus sign, which in arithmetic means take away

explanation.surface: An oriental ghost is spotted placing an order, and we are asked what it wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges SEEN as NESE. The printed dash is read as a minus sign, spoken as 'take away'. 'this?' points to the whole clue as the thing being ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's own scene, someone placing an order with a Far Eastern flavour, describes a meal delivered from a Cantonese restaurant.

clue.text: Fruit: a few squashes shattered crate

indicators.note: the number presses the broken letters inside itself

parts.note: nine is a loose handful of items, read here as a few

indicators.note: a shattered crate is in pieces, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Some soft fruit squashed when the crate broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges crate and 'squashes' presses those letters inside the number. Calling nine 'a few' is a stretch the setter allows himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned peach variety is a stone fruit eaten fresh.

clue.text: A social shame

parts.note: a social is a party, informally a bash

explanation.surface: A party that turned into an embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to make someone feel embarrassed or humiliated.

clue.text: See 22
Keen to get type of melon in freezer

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to cry
the Ogen is a small sweet melon variety

explanation.surface: Someone eager to put a melon into the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' is the verb to wail, not the adjective eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerant producing extremely low temperatures is a substance used for freezing.

clue.text: Dance tour

definitions.meaning: to step lightly, as in 'the light fantastic'

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a light dancing step and a short journey or outing.

clue.text: Factory where fishwife feeds birds

indicators.note: the fish and wife are fed into the birds, placed inside them

parts.note: storks are large wading birds
split as fish and wife: an eel is a fish and W abbreviates wife

explanation.surface: A fishwife feeding the birds, as though at a seaside factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishwife' must be split into its two halves; a fishwife is a woman who sells fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where iron is smelted into metal is an industrial works.

clue.text: Statesman's charity rolling in money once

definitions.note: read as 'man of a US state is', the 's being is

indicators.note: the charity sits in the coin, as one is rolling in money

parts.note: the florin was a British two-shilling coin before decimal currency

indicators.note: the charity turns over and is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help given charitably

explanation.surface: A politician's charity is awash with old money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' is a punning label for a man from an American state, not a politician. The florin was a pre-decimal British two-shilling coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Florida is a man of one of the American states, a cryptic sense of the word.

clue.text: Somewhat head over heels, supermodels go doolally for a slipper

indicators.note: head over heels says the hidden letters are read backwards
Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Models going crazy, falling in love for a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', which is a link word; 'a slipper' alone stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge pulled by huskies slides over snow, so it is something that slips along.

clue.text: Filthy wet hole turns dry when raked back

indicators.note: the pieces are drawn backwards, read from right to left

parts.note: tips, as a container turns over
sec describes dry wine

explanation.surface: A dirty pit dries out once raked over.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit for sewage or waste is a foul, damp hole in the ground.

clue.text: Force party to bind over leaders in criminal investigation

indicators.note: the party wraps round the other pieces, binding them

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
o'er is the poetic contraction of over

indicators.note: the first letters of the following words lead them

explanation.surface: A party forced to bind someone over in a criminal case.
explanation.walkthrough: To bind over is a British court order to keep the peace; here it splits apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Compelling someone by threats or pressure is the use of force.

clue.text: Colonist possibly into homely tropical food

indicators.note: the insect goes into the other word

parts.note: homely means plain, unattractive
ants live in colonies, so one may be a colonist

explanation.surface: A settler sitting down to some simple tropical fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy banana-like fruit cooked as a staple across the tropics.

clue.text: Marked danger branding a horse

indicators.note: branding marks a horse's hide, so the danger is set into it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
risk means danger

explanation.surface: Branding a horse is risky work, leaving it marked.
explanation.definitionFit: Text flagged with a little star symbol has been marked out.

clue.text: Windy US soldier dropping trousers

indicators.note: as a verb, trousers means pockets, so the soldier goes inside

parts.note: an animal dropping is a turd
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier suffering wind as his trousers come down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets, and 'dropping' a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy speech is pompous and inflated, and so is a bombastic style.

clue.text: South American relations divided county

parts.note: US is American, as in US troops
sexual relations, or sex

explanation.surface: Relations between South Americans split the county.
explanation.walkthrough: This English county is split into East and West halves for local government.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-coast English shire has two administrative parts, so it is a split shire.

clue.text: 23 7, would you say?

parts.note: spoken aloud, the two answers 23 and 7 sound like someone who arranges loans

explanation.walkthrough: The answers at 23 and 7 together sound like 'loan arranger', a jokey name for a lender at a high-street branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The official at a high-street branch who approves loans is the classic arranger of borrowing.

clue.text: Independent type left a note in the past

parts.note: a oner was slang for the old one-pound note

explanation.surface: Someone independent who once left a banknote behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The British one-pound note was withdrawn in 1988, hence 'in the past'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who prefers their own company is self-reliant and solitary.

clue.text: Exchanges full of invective, primarily?

indicators.note: the exchanges hold the letter inside

parts.note: trades are exchanges of goods

indicators.note: first, so only the initial letter of invective is taken

explanation.surface: Rows in which insults fly, and they are mostly abusive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches of denunciation are bursts of abusive language.

clue.text: Recollection of island monster gripping a nation

indicators.note: the reversed pieces grip the letter a inside them
read as re-collection, gathering the pieces up again backwards

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
an orc is a monster of fantasy

explanation.surface: Memories of a sea monster from an island, clutching a whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollection of' reverses the two pieces (read it as re-collection), and 'gripping' puts A in the middle. An ait, or eyot, is a little island in the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan republic on the Adriatic is an independent country.

clue.text: Board getting the nod in Strasbourg — and further east?

parts.note: yes in French, Strasbourg being a French city
farther east, in Germany, yes is ja

explanation.surface: A board game that gets approval in Alsace and beyond.
explanation.walkthrough: Strasbourg sits on the Rhine border, so 'further east' is across it in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettered board used at seances to spell out supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: I create when intoxicated, penning very obscure stuff

indicators.note: the jumbled letters write around, enclosing the other piece
drunk words stumble, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A writer claims to produce when drunk, writing obscure material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when intoxicated' turns I CREATE into ETERICA, which 'penning' wraps round SO after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite items understood by only a few specialists are arcane material.
